response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 GROUP BY orderslink), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM per_order) SELECT p.orderslink, p.avg_rebtotal, p.avg_ratio, CASE WHEN o.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL THEN p.avg_ratio / NULLIF(o.mean_ratio, 0) END AS relative_ratio FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY (CASE WHEN o.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL AND p.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END), relative_ratio DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A feerate of 0 is treated as a missing ratio (NULLIF) so the division does not error; such rows are ignored by the average.
Fee rows with a NULL orderslink are grouped together as one group, since the request does not say to exclude them.
The overall mean is the unweighted mean of per-order average ratios, taken over orders whose average ratio is not NULL, computed after the rebrate > 0.0005 filter and before the LIMIT.
